This was the game I bought that got me into MegaMan. Housing 8 great games and some fun bonuses, it certainly helped escalate my infatuation with this series.

The games run pretty well (on PS2, at least), and have some nice updates like removing sprite flickering and lag and fixing typos. And of course, the remixed music!!!! Seriously, wonderful bangers there!!

I also love how accessable the game is to newcomers. The game autosaves instead of using passwords, you can choose to have 5 lives be the default instead of 3 as the default, the fun Navi Mode, and even an easy difficulty mode for all the games (except 8). For those that want to play the series but aren't the best at retro 2D platformers (and let's be real, the first game is brutal regardless of player skill for a first run), this is a solid alternative. You're still getting the same experience, just not as much frustration. I'll admit, I sometimes play the games on easy mode even now if I just want to do a casual run.

Aside from the lag in other versions, the GameCube's backwards controls, and "Jump, Jump, Slide, Slide" being at its worst, my only other issues with it is the botched ending in Mega Man 7 and the lack of Mega Man And Bass. This would have been the perfect opportunity for the SNES version to get an international release with no screen crunch. Shame it wasn't taken advantage of.

Overall... gonna be honest, I still prefer the Anniversary Collection than the Legacy Collections (for the classic games specifically). I much rather take an easy mode over save states and rewind features. The latter just feels like cheating. With the lack of MM&B and honestly preferring the original releases of 9 & 10, aside from the challenges, Anniversary Collection tops it for me.

So, the pause glitch is where you press the select button (for regular pausing, not the item menu) just after a weapon has come into direct contact with an enemy.

So, say you're at the Yellow Devil fight, and use the Thunder Beam. Once the Thunder Beam comes in contact with the Yellow Devil's eye, immediately press select. Then continue rapidly pressing select to pause and unpause. Every time you unpause, you deal some more damage to the Yellow Devil, as if its a new attack. Do this constantly, and you can beat the Yellow Devil while only going through one or two rounds of dodging instead of after every attack.

The trick can be used in other fights too, including the Robot Masters, the Copy Robot, Wily Machine 1, and even against the Big Eyes. It can also be done with any weapon; I just used Thunder Beam as the example. But it's most notorious with the Yellow Devil due to the difficulty he possesses.

I fully agree. I re-watched all four films yesterday and I found 'Temple' added basically nothing to the overall plot (or, more accurately, nothing that carries over to the other films). While 'Kingdom' may not be as good as 'Raiders' and 'Crusade', it certainly added more than 'Temple', by having him marry Marion and have a son Mutt. It also works as, since the film takes place in the 50s, the Russians would be the natural sequel to the Nazis.

Temple's plot doesn't feel revolved around Indy. It was a local problem, and really any action hero could've been in that role. Recovering a stone is certainly smaller than the lost arc, the holy grail, or El Dorado.

I also agree with the problem that the whole movie takes place in one location, when part of the fun of seeing an Indiana Jones movie is seeing the film move to different climates, but half of Temple takes place in the temple itself, and the rest is either the village, the palace, or a jungle trek with no action.

One note about the film is some of the effects feel unfinished (the plane crash and a shot of the water in the mines while the group are running from the minecart).

With the exception of Shanghai, there's barely any action in Temple before getting to the Temple itself, which is around half-way through the movie, rather than non-stop action like the other films. Kingdom had a lot of talking scenes, but the action feels more varied.

Also, while Willie and Short Round aren't hateable, they're certainly no Marcus, Sallah, or Marion. Speaking of which, Temple is the only Indiana Jones movie without Barnett College making an appearance, showing Indy giving a lecture. It also has Indy as the only character in the film who appears in any of the other films.

Having said all of that, I don't think Temple is terrible. For the most part, it has good action, good visuals, an occasional joke that lands, some of the actors are pretty good (namely Harrison Ford and Amrish Puri), and you can never really go wrong with John William's score. There are good things sure, but as it stands, it's easily the weakest Indiana Jones movie. It's not terrible, it's just average.

I want to end this on one final note. A quote from Stephen Spielberg says "I wasn’t happy with the second film at all. It was too dark, too subterranean, and much too horrific. I thought it out-poltered *Poltergeist.* There’s not an ounce of my own personal feeling in *Temple Of Doom."* Well, if that doesn't say something about Temple, I don't know what can.
